briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Cannabis Wins in the Courtroom and on the Judges' Table While National Deal-Making and Psychedelics Surge
briefs.top: Michigan operators notch real wins this week — a Sixth Circuit reversal wiping out a $31.8M judgment, a new dispensary-cap vote on the ballot, and top-shelf Michigan flower crowned at the 'Grammys of Cannabis' — even as the fight over the 24% wholesale tax now runs straight through the governor's race. Nationally, Curaleaf's bold bid for Aurora Cannabis and Vireo's dispensary-buying spree show MSOs are back on offense, while Compass Pathways and the FDA push psychedelic medicine closer to market.

local.text: Michigan flower takes top honors at 2026 Zalympix — Mitten Canna Co.'s Toad Venom won best overall flower and Detroit's Hytek topped the rosin category with Oishii Piña at the state's 'Grammys of Cannabis' in Pontiac.

Michigan cannabis sales cross $17 billion since legalization — cumulative adult-use and medical sales have generated an estimated $2.66 billion in state taxes, with August alone adding $259 million in demand.

Appeals court erases $31.8M cannabis judgment tied to Curaleaf — the Sixth Circuit reportedly voided the contract-dispute award, clearing a major liability off the books for one of the state's biggest operators.
Menominee could add four new dispensary licenses this fall — voters decide Nov. 3 on raising the city's cap from 9 to 13 after a judge cleared the ballot measure for the general election.

Industry group bets on a governor who'll kill the wholesale tax — MiCIA endorsed Republican John James over his pledge to repeal the 24% levy, giving operators a concrete political path toward relief.

national.text: Curaleaf goes big with a $270M bid for Aurora Cannabis — the MSO's unsolicited cross-border offer topped out near $5/share, signaling renewed appetite for consolidation despite the board's rejection.
Vireo Growth's buying spree targets roughly 270 dispensary doors — new deals with FLUENT and C21, plus a merger with Planet 13, push the fast-rising MSO deeper into Florida and Nevada.

Compass Pathways closes in on its FDA filing for psilocybin therapy — the company is nearing completion of its rolling NDA for COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, targeting a U.S. launch in 2027.

FDA holds a landmark hearing on psychedelic medicine's future — regulators convened public testimony on the potential future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs, a step advocates see as building toward broader approval pathways.
Federal legalization bill picks up its 18th Senate co-sponsor — bipartisan momentum keeps building in Congress even as DEA's broader Schedule III rulemaking grinds through its own hearing process.
